title: Summit HVAC — discovery-led call that closes
description: Rep (Maya, Relay) runs proper discovery with Dan, ops manager at an 18-tech HVAC company. Pain is quantified, budget and decision process surface, a price question is handled with ROI, and the call ends with a verbal commitment to a paid pilot.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Hi Dan, Maya from Relay. Thanks for making time, I know Tuesdays are hectic for dispatch.

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Ha, you have no idea. Yeah, happy to chat, I've got about thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Perfect, I'll keep us on track. Before I say anything about Relay, can you walk me through how scheduling works at Summit today, start to finish?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Sure. So we've got eighteen techs across two branches. Every evening our dispatcher, Carla, builds the next day's board in a spreadsheet and texts each tech their route. Then the day starts and everything changes.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: What's the most painful part of that for you?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Same-day changes. A job runs long, a part isn't on the truck, a customer cancels. Carla is on the phone nonstop re-shuffling. Last month we double-booked two techs to the same address twice.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That sounds exhausting for her. When a job runs late, what happens to the customers further down the route?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Honestly, they get a call if Carla remembers. Half the time they don't, and then they call us angry. We've had a couple of one-star reviews that say exactly that.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Roughly how many hours a week would you say Carla spends on the manual re-shuffling and those calls?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Probably three hours a day on the bad days. Call it twelve to fifteen hours a week, and that's on top of her normal work.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: And the double bookings and missed windows, do you have a sense of how many jobs a month you lose or have to redo because of that?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: We tracked it in April. Nine jobs we had to reschedule or eat a discount on. Average ticket is around four hundred dollars, so it adds up.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: So call it three to four thousand a month in slipped revenue plus most of a part-time salary in Carla's hours. Does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Yeah, that's about right. When you say it like that it's worse than I thought.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: What made you take this call now, of all times?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Summer. We go from eighteen to about twenty-four techs with seasonal hires in June, and Carla told me flat out she can't do another summer on the spreadsheet. She'd probably quit.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Got it, so there's a real clock on this. If you had something in place before June, what would good look like for you?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Carla builds the board in ten minutes instead of two hours, techs get updates on their phones automatically, and customers get a text when we're running late so they stop calling us.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That's very close to what Relay does day to day. Let me describe it briefly and then you tell me where it falls short. Relay builds the daily board from your job list and tech skills, re-dispatches automatically when a job runs long, pushes the change to the tech's app, and texts the customer an updated window. Which of those matters most to you?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: The automatic re-dispatch and the customer text. That's the part that's killing us. Does it handle two branches with separate territories?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: It does, each branch gets its own board and dispatcher view, with shared techs if you want. How do you handle techs crossing branches today?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Badly. We try not to. But in summer we have to. Okay, this is interesting. What does something like this cost?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Before I give you a number, can I ask what you're spending today on scheduling, including Carla's time and the dispatch add-on on your current accounting software?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: The add-on is about two hundred a month and we barely use it. Carla's time on this is probably another fifteen hundred a month if I'm honest. We hadn't set a formal budget, but I've got discretion up to about a thousand a month without going to the owner.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That's helpful. For eighteen to twenty-four techs Relay is eleven hundred a month on the annual plan, which includes the customer texting and both branches. So against the roughly five thousand a month you just described in slipped jobs and hours, it pays for itself in the first week of each month.

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Eleven hundred. Okay. That's a bit over my line but not by much. The owner, Greg, would need to sign off on anything over a thousand, but he and I decide this kind of thing together and he's aware of the Carla situation.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Good to know. How did the last software purchase like this get approved on your side, what did Greg want to see?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: He wanted to see it actually work with our jobs, not a canned demo. And he wanted a way out if it didn't.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That's fair, and it's how most of our HVAC customers start. We can run a two-week paid pilot on one branch, using your real job list, with a full refund if Carla isn't building the board faster by day ten. Would that give Greg what he needs?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Yeah, that's exactly the kind of thing he'd say yes to. What does the pilot involve on our side?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: About an hour with Carla to import jobs and techs, then she runs her normal day in Relay with me on a shared channel for the first three days. The techs just install the app.

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: That's manageable. Carla would love that, honestly. The app part might get some grumbling from the older guys but they'll get over it.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: We see that a lot. Would it help if we did the first tech onboarding in person at your morning huddle?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: That would help a lot, yes.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: So if I've got this right: the main problem is same-day re-dispatch and customer communication, it costs you around five thousand a month today, you need it in place before June when the seasonal techs start, and Greg needs to see it work on real jobs with a way out. Did I miss anything?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: No, that's it exactly. You've listened better than the last two vendors I talked to.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Given the June timing, how about we start the pilot the week after next? I can send the pilot agreement tonight, and I'd love fifteen minutes with you and Greg on Thursday to walk through it together.

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Thursday works. Greg's usually in by nine. Let's do Thursday at nine thirty.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Booked. And if Greg's comfortable on Thursday, is there anything else that would stop us starting the pilot the following Monday?

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: No. Honestly, if Greg's in, let's do it. Send the agreement over and I'll get Carla to block that hour.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Fantastic. I'll send the agreement and a one-page summary of the numbers we discussed within the hour. Thanks Dan, this was a great conversation.

utterances.speaker: prospect
utterances.text: Thanks Maya. Talk Thursday.
